en: The Ritual for Praising, Paying Homage to, and Repenting before Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, Explained by the Bodhisattva Śrāmaṇera Guwu Zhixu.

(The practitioner, having purified body, speech, and mind, stands before the sacred image and should reflect: "I and all sentient beings have accumulated delusions and committed transgressions, leaving us without rescue or refuge. May the Great Being’s vast compassion serve as our refuge and our rescue. Furthermore, one should contemplate the Dharma-body of the Great Being and his ten... [text continues]

The essence of the Three Jewels is eternally pervasive and omnipresent; it is non-dual and equal to my own present mind-nature. Generate deep faith and understanding, as if beholding a compassionate countenance. Spread your sitting mat, stand with palms joined in reverence, and chant:

With all reverence and single-minded devotion, prostrate to the eternally abiding Triple Gem of the ten directions. (Having performed one general prostration, hold incense and flowers with solemnity and make offerings according to the Dharma, chanting:
May these clouds of incense and flowers pervade the worlds of the ten directions, making offerings to all Buddhas, the Honored Dharma, and all the worthy sages.
Throughout boundless Buddha-fields, may they perform the work of Buddhas. (At this point, cease chanting; burn incense and scatter flowers, and with focused visualization, say:
May all the Jewels of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha be eternally omnipresent and nowhere absent.

By means of this incense and these flowers, may they become equal to the nature of reality (*dharmatā*), universally perfuming all Buddha-fields to perform the work of Buddhas throughout the ten directions.
There is no time when all manner of offerings do not exist.

I shall now, with all the various kinds of incense, flowers, necklaces, banners, flags, precious canopies, and all manner of exquisite ornaments; with various kinds of music, lamps, candles, and fires;
and with food, drink, clothing, bedding, and medicine—indeed, with everything that exists throughout the entirety of the ten directions—[make these offerings].
With various articles of adornment and offerings, I mentally envision them from afar and, together with all sentient beings, offer them as a dedication.
In all worlds, those who practice such offerings, I now rejoice in;
those who have not yet practiced them, may they be inspired and guided to do so. Furthermore, may my own body swiftly reach everywhere throughout the [ten] directions.
In every buddha-field, at each instance of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, one should, together with all sentient beings,
offer up all manner of adorned articles of worship. One should make offerings to the dharma-body, form-body, and śarīra images of all Buddhas,
as well as to their stūpas, temples, and towers, and to all Buddhist activities— offering to everything that is worthy of veneration.
There is the Dharma-treasury and the place where the Dharma is preached. One makes offerings to all the assemblies of worthy and holy ones (āryasaṃgha).
Having made such offerings together with all sentient beings, one gradually achieves the six pāramitās and the four immeasurable minds (catur-apramāṇa).
One deeply realizes that all dharmas are originally quiescent, without arising or ceasing, and of a single flavor and equality.
Free from conceptual thought and pure, ultimately perfect. (Having finished the visualization, arise and say:
Having made these offerings, with all reverence. (After one prostration, again join the palms and praise, saying:)
Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha. By means of his supernormal powers, he manifests in the form of a śrāvaka.
He is a treasury of all subtle and wondrous merits; he is the source from which the jewels of liberation emerge; he is the clear and pure eye of all bodhisattvas;
he is the leader of the merchants journeying toward nirvāṇa. Like a wish-fulfilling jewel, he rains down all manner of wealth and treasures according to one's aspirations.
They fulfill all who seek; they illuminate those who practice virtue like the bright sun; they light the way for those who have lost their path like a brilliant torch;
they remove the heat of afflictions like the coolness of the moon; they serve as a bridge for those crossing the four currents; they act as a boat or raft for those hastening to the further shore;
they subdue all non-Buddhists like a lion king; and they conquer all celestial Māras like a great dragon.
Like an elephant, he protects against all fears as a kinsman or friend; he wards off all enemies like a moat or a city wall; he rescues from all perils and hardships like a father or mother;
he shelters the timid and weak like a thicket of trees. He causes the roots of goodness in sentient beings not to decay;
he manifests wondrous realms to cause the multitude to rejoice; he exhorts sentient beings to increase their sense of shame and remorse; and he leads them to seek merit and wisdom.
This causes one to be fully adorned and enables the effortless turning of the Great Wheel of Dharma. His supreme merits cannot be measured;
having long cultivated firm great vows and great compassion, his courageous diligence surpasses that of all other bodhisattvas.
By taking refuge with a sincere mind for even the duration of a single meal, reciting his name, prostrating, and making offerings, one can cause all beings to be freed from sorrow.
Suffering! May all your aspirations be swiftly fulfilled; may you be established upon the path to rebirth in the heavens and to *nirvāṇa*.
Therefore, with single-minded devotion, I take refuge and pay homage. (Having offered praise, perform one prostration, add incense to show respect, and chant:)

With single-minded devotion, prostrate to the Original Teacher, Śākyamuni Tathāgata. (Bowing down, contemplate and say: “The nature of the one who prostrates and the object of prostration is empty and quiescent; the mutual resonance of cause and response is inconceivable.

My place of practice is like a jewel of Indra, within which the reflection of Śākyamuni Tathāgata appears. My own body and shadow appear before the Tathāgata; with head touching his feet, I take refuge and pay homage. The following [prostrations] shall follow this same pattern, changing only the name of the Buddha.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Tathāgata Lion’s Vigorous Stride Endowed with Myriad Practices and to the Tathāgata Sovereign King of the Samādhi of Awakening Flowers.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Tathāgata Accomplished in All-Knowledge and to the Tathāgata Pure Lotus Sun.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Tathāgata Anantagātra, the Tathāgata Ratnagotra, the Tathāgata Padmottara,
and the Tathāgata Siṃhanāda. With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Tathāgata Ratnajaya, the Tathāgata Ratnalakṣaṇa, the Tathāgata Kāṣāyadhvaja, and Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū.

Homage to the Tathāgata King. With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Buddha Pure Moon, the Buddha Mountain King, the Buddha Supreme Wisdom, the Buddha King of Pure Radiance, the Buddha Accomplished Wisdom,
the Buddha Unsurpassed, the Buddha Wondrous Sound, the Buddha Full Moon, and the Buddha Moon Face— such as these, beyond description.
I single-mindedly prostrate to all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas: to Krakucchanda Buddha, Vipaśyin Buddha, and the other seven Buddhas, the Tathāgatas;
and I single-mindedly prostrate to the fifty-three Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, beginning with Samantaprabhāsa Buddha.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to all the Tathāgatas of the past, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the assembly in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven Palace, and to all the Tathāgas of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds gathered from the ten directions.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Tathāgata Formless One (Animitta) of the Blissful Eon in the future Pure Abode World,
as well as to all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to all the physical bodies, *śarīra*, images, stupas, temples, and towers, and to all the Buddha-works of the Buddhas of the ten directions.

(Contemplate thus: "The Dharma-body of the Buddhas is like space; their manifested activities abide in the world beyond thought. Before these manifestations appear, I take refuge in and pay homage to each and every one of them.")

With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the *Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva’s Sūtra on Fundamental Vows*, the *Mahāyāna Mahāsannipāta Kṣitigarbha Daśacakrakṣepaṇa Sūtra*, the *Sūtra on Examining the Retribution of Good and Evil Karma*, and all the Dharma-treasuries of the ten directions and the three periods of time. (Three prostrations in total. Contemplate thus:

The true emptiness of the Dharma-realm is like space; the eternally abiding Dharma-jewel is inconceivable. I appear as reflections before all these Dharma-jewels; there is none to which I do not pay homage with my life.)
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, the Bodhisattva Vasumitra, and the Mahāsattva Samādhi-viśeṣa-rāja.
(Visualize these verses as being from the Buddha, merely changing the names of the bodhisattvas; all subsequent instances follow this pattern.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati, the Bodhisattva Vimukti, and the Mahāsattva Samantabhadra.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva Puguang, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, and the Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha. With single-minded devotion,
I pay homage to the Bodhisattva Haojiwen, the Bodhisattva Maitreya, the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha, and the Bodhisattva Sthitaviśuddhi.
The faithful Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva single-mindedly prostrates to all Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
Single-mindedly prostrating, he pays homage to the Venerable Kauṇḍinya, the Venerable Upāli, and the Venerable Maudgalyāyana. One...
With one mind, we prostrate to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, who has manifested divided bodies and gathered from within the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.
With one mind, we prostrate to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, who manifests in the form of a śrāvaka within this great assembly.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, who provides excellent consolation as taught in the *Sūtra of the Divination of the Grounds*.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, who enters the samādhi that awakens wisdom.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, who has entered the samādhi of fully endowed, boundless wisdom.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, who has entered the samādhi of fully endowed, pure wisdom.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, who has entered the samādhi of wisdom endowed with perfect shame and remorse.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, who has entered the samādhi of illumination endowed with all vehicles.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha who has entered the Samādhi of the Radiance of the Supernormal Power of Entering into Sorrowlessness.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha who has entered the Samādhi of the Radiance of the Perfectly Endowed Supreme Supernormal Powers.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha who has entered the Samādhi of Universally Illuminating All Worlds.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha who has entered the Samādhi of the Radiant Lamp of All Buddhas.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha who has entered the Samādhi of Entering Vajra-Light.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha who has entered the Samādhi of the Intellect’s Power that is Difficult to Subdue.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha who has entered the Samādhi of Entering Lightning Radiance.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha who has entered the Samādhi of Possessing the Most Exquisite Flavors.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha who has entered the samādhi of the supreme, perfect vital energy.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha who has entered the samādhi of all sublime requisites.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, who has entered the samādhi of non-contentious wisdom.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, who has entered the samādhi that induces supreme exultation.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, who has entered the Samādhi of the Radiance of the Path to Fulfillment.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, who has entered the Samādhi of the Supreme Vajra of Excellent Abiding.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha who has entered the Samādhi of the Supreme Banner of Superior Contemplation.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha who has entered the Samādhi of the Sound Endowed with Compassion.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha who enters the Samādhi that Gathers All Merits.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha who enters the Samādhi of Oceanic Lightning Light.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, who is able to enter samādhis as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and brings all sentient beings to maturity.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, who, by means of the power of various samādhis, eliminates the kalpa of weapons.
With single-minded devotion, prostrate to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, who, by means of various powers of meditative concentration, eliminates the kalpa of disease.
With single-minded devotion, prostrate to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, who, by means of various powers of meditative concentration, eliminates the kalpa of famine.
(Having completed the prostrations as before, and finished reciting the verse, one further reflects thus:)
I and all sentient beings have, since beginningless time, been constantly obstructed by the heavy offenses of the three karmas and six sense organs.
We have failed to see the Buddhas and remain ignorant of the essential means of liberation; we merely follow the cycle of birth and death, unaware of the wondrous principle.

Although I now know it, I still share with all sentient beings the state of being obstructed by every kind of heavy offense. Now, before Kṣitigarbha and the Buddhas of the ten directions, universally...

For the sake of all sentient beings, I take refuge and repent. I pray that you will grant your protection and cause all obstacles to be extinguished. (Having formed this thought, kneel on the right knee and proclaim:)
For the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm, I vow that they shall all sever the three obstructions. I take refuge and repent.

(Having chanted this, prostrate with the five limbs touching the ground, and further reflect: From beginningless time until now, I and all sentient beings, due to craving and false views, have internally clung to the notions of self and person (1), externally associated with evil friends (2), and failed to rejoice in even a hair’s breadth of another’s goodness (3), doing so solely through the three karmas.
1. Extensively committing various transgressions (4). 2. Although the acts were not extensive, the evil mind was pervasive (5). 3. Continuing day and night without interruption (6). 4.
Concealing and denying one's faults, unwilling to let others know (7). 5. Having no fear of the evil realms (8). 6. Lacking shame and a sense of propriety (9). 7.
Denying the existence of cause and effect (10). Therefore, on this day, I have come to deeply believe in cause and effect (1). [The state of] being born... (2)
1. Intense shame and remorse (2). 2. Giving rise to great fear (3). 3. Confessing and repenting openly (4). 4. Severing the continuity of the mind (5).
6. Generate the bodhicitta and sever evil while cultivating goodness. 7. Diligently restrain the three karmas to overturn past grave transgressions. 8.

Rejoice in even a hair’s breadth of merit, whether from ordinary beings or sages. 9. Contemplate that the Buddhas of the ten directions possess great merit and wisdom, capable of rescuing and delivering myself and all sentient beings, placing us upon the shore of the three virtues from the sea of the two deaths. Since beginningless time, [I have been...]
[One] knew that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is empty and quiescent, yet [previously] committed manifold evils.

Now, knowing them to be empty and quiescent, for the sake of seeking Bodhi and for the sake of sentient beings, one extensively cultivates all manner of goodness and universally severs all evils (10).
I only pray that Kṣitigarbha, with his compassion, will accept me. (Having formed this thought, one should rise to kneel on the right knee and proclaim:)

I, [Name], a disciple, together with all sentient beings of the Dharma-realm, sincerely repent. Since we were deluded regarding the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), we have pointlessly undergone the cycle of birth and death (*saṃsāra*).

With ignorance (*avidyā*) shrouding our minds, we did not know the essential means of escape. Clinging to pride in our own cleverness while being truly foolish, we heard the Mahāyāna teachings and erroneously gave rise to a nihilistic understanding.
We repudiated cause and effect, severed our roots of goodness, and became estranged from right faith. We remained estranged...
Regarding right aspiration: being devoid of right intention and right view; distancing oneself from virtuous friends, favorable places, and auspicious times;

remaining far removed from pure ethical discipline, right concentration, and right wisdom; following after evil associates; giving rise to various false views; and committing immeasurable karmic offenses of body, speech, and mind;
or further slandering the sublime Dharma of the Mahāyāna, or slandering the vehicle of the Pratyekabuddhas, or furthermore—

They slander the vehicle of the śrāvakas, obstructing, defiling, and concealing it so that it does not circulate. Furthermore, regarding those disciples of the Buddhas— whether they are vessels for the Dharma or not,
whether they possess the precepts or have broken them, even down to those who are without precepts but wear a fragment of the *kāṣāya* and have shaved their hair and beards—
they frequently act with anger and resentment, reviling, insulting, ridiculing, slandering, and concealing the virtues of others.
10. Proclaiming evil: using harsh and abusive speech; threatening, intimidating, and coercing; striking with clubs and inflicting injury;

plundering the alms bowl; plundering the necessities of life; cutting off food and drink; forcing one to return to lay life; stripping away the *kāṣāya*; binding with shackles and fetters; imprisoning in a dungeon;
treating with contempt and causing provocation so as to bring about unhappiness; and seizing *stūpas* and the property of the Saṃgha. These are the ten unwholesome actions (*daśākuśala*).
From the five heinous crimes down to the icchantikas, by virtue of these karmic conditions, they fall into the various evil realms for immeasurable kalpas,
traversing the three miserable paths and undergoing all manner of suffering that is difficult to describe in words of agony. Even if they should encounter immeasurable Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas,
personally receiving their offerings and making public confession to eliminate their transgressions, and further upholding immeasurable dharmas of the Path and practicing them;
Through immeasurable difficult practices and ascetic austerities, because certain karmic obstructions remain unexhausted,
we have been unable to realize the bliss of *nirvāṇa*, nor have we been able to realize the sublime merits of the gates of *samādhi*.
We now turn toward the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha and all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and resolve upon the Mahāyāna mind to propagate the teachings of the Tathāgata.
In order that the lineage of the Triple Gem in this land may flourish with majestic power and endure for a long time in the world;
in order to utterly destroy the firm afflictions of all sentient beings so that none remain; and to inspire in all sentient beings a profound sense of shame and remorse.
I openly confess and repent, seeking their complete eradication.

I only pray that the Great Compassionate Honored Ones of the ten directions, as well as the Great Being Kṣitigarbha, will take pity upon us and protect us, delivering and uprooting us so that these karmic obstacles may all be extinguished, and we shall never again undergo the bitter fruits of suffering in the evil realms. We now, before [the Buddhas]...
Before the World-Honored One and the Great Beings, with a sincere heart, they made this true vow:
"From this day forth until we attain Bodhi, may we never encounter such evil conditions; may we resolutely refrain from committing such grave offenses;
may we never slander the True Dharma of the Buddhas; may we never disturb or annoy those who have left the household life; and may we certainly never destroy the [eyes of sentient beings]."
The Dharma-eye arises, and the lineage of the Three Jewels is neither severed nor extinguished.
We pray that the World-Honored One and the Great Beings will graciously accept and bear witness to these vows we have made,
so that we may quickly accomplish the ten dharmas and the ten wheels, attain the dharma-patience of the faultless true path, and [attain] the three vehicles within the three vehicles.
One will never err regarding those who are not vessels for the Dharma. In the Mahāyāna teachings, one will advance without regression.
One’s sharp wisdom and supreme merit will constantly increase. One will swiftly attain mastery over all meditative concentrations, dhāraṇīs, patiences, and stages.
One will always encounter virtuous spiritual friends and never be separated from the vision of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
The Śrāvaka disciples of Sa will not be separated from hearing the Dharma, nor from attending upon and making offerings to the Saṃgha.
They will always be able to exert diligence in all roots of goodness and possess a mind that is never weary of the practices and vows for Bodhi.

They will destroy, shatter, and extinguish previously committed evils, swiftly realizing the unsurpassed Wheel of Dharma. Through skillful means, they will bring sentient beings to maturity, causing them all to attain [enlightenment].
May you obtain benefit and peace. (Recite either once or three times. Then stand up and proclaim:

Having finished the confession and the making of vows, I take refuge and pay homage to the Triple Gem. (After one prostration, stand up again. Straighten your body and direct your thoughts so that all the Triple Gems pervade the void.

Visualize them seated upon their Dharma thrones. Turn your body one by one, circumambulating according to the ritual. Regard this body as a shadow and its voice as an echo, pervading the ten directions. Above, make offerings to the Triple Gem; below, awaken the multitude of spirits. Do not allow the mind to scatter, and chant with harmony and elegance:)
Homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions. Homage to the Dharma of the ten directions. Homage to the Sangha of the ten directions.
Homage to our Original Teacher, Śākyamuni Buddha.
Homage to the *Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva’s Sūtra on His Fundamental Vows*.
Homage to the Mahāyāna Mahāsannipāta Kṣitigarbha Daśacakrakṣepaṇa Sūtra.
Homage to the Divination of Good and Evil Karmic Retribution Sūtra.

Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha. (Recite this three times or seven times. Having completed the circumambulation, turn back toward the Dharma seat, stand upright, and with a sincere mind, chant:)
Taking refuge in the Buddha, may all sentient beings realize the Great Way and give rise to the unsurpassed mind.
Taking refuge in the Dharma, may all sentient beings enter deeply into the treasury of the scriptures, with wisdom as vast as the ocean.
Taking refuge in the Sangha, may all sentient beings lead and manage the great assembly, free from all hindrances.

I pay homage to the noble assembly. (Having finished the inquiry after the greeting, proceed next to the quiet chamber. There, one may either recite the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, or maintain the mantra for extinguishing karma, or contemplate the Great Being’s impartial Dharmakāya, or practice the two types of contemplative paths such as "Mind-Only Consciousness.
If one is solely faithful and resolute, then one will certainly be able to extinguish obstacles and will certainly realize the patience of the Dharma.)
Postscript: Alas!
The Great Dharma has long been obscured, and many people harbor erroneous understandings. Clinging to the Mahāyāna while slandering the Hīnayāna, this is the case throughout the world.
Who knows that the manifold sufferings of hell will follow in their wake? And the retribution of being mute and speechless is even more difficult to fathom. Therefore, I—
The World-Honored One of Great Compassion, Kṣitigarbha, manifested in the form of a śrāvaka within a great assembly.
Therein, the World-Honored One extensively extolled his supreme virtues and made a comparison, saying:

"Suppose there were someone who, for a hundred kalpas, [made offerings] at the abodes of as many great bodhisattvas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River—such as Maitreya, Mañjuśrī, Avalokiteśvara, Samantabhadra, and others—"

To take refuge in the mind, recite its name, pay homage, and make offerings while seeking all one's wishes is not as effective as for someone who, for the duration of a single meal, takes refuge in, recites the name of, pays homage to, and makes offerings to Kṣitigarbha.
This is because the Bodhisattva has long cultivated firm great vows and great compassion.
His courageous diligence surpasses that of all other bodhisattvas. Indeed, in these末代 (final) times, it is very easy to merely speak of the Mahāyāna;
however, to personally practice the monastic conduct is truly difficult. How could one know that abandoning the Hīnayāna while discoursing on the Mahāyāna renders even that Mahāyāna non-existent?

Conversely, how could one know that awakening to the Mahāyāna while employing the Hīnayāna renders even that Hīnayāna itself Mahāyāna? Therefore, the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* warns against [such superficiality] in its propagation.

The sūtras must necessarily rely upon the four modes of peaceful and happy conduct (*caturvidha-sukha-vihāra*). The *Nirvāṇa Sūtra* speaks of the eternal Buddha-nature in its ultimate discourse and especially upholds the precepts and discipline.
Is it not the case that the Great Being’s merit is so exceptionally flourishing precisely because of this? Zhi Xu deeply regrets his evil habits from previous lives;

in his youth, he forcefully reviled the Triple Gem and committed the karma of immediate retribution. It was only by relying on the fact that his roots of goodness had not yet perished that he was saved.

Having been able to hear this Honored Scripture of the Original Vow, I came to know that there exists a supreme filial piety that transcends the mundane world; thus, my perverse views were overturned and right faith was born within me.
Nevertheless, due to the residual karma of having slandered the Dharma, although I have practiced with diligent toil, I have not yet attained the stage of Dharma-patience (*dharmakṣānti*).
Every time I open and read the three scriptures of the Great Being, I cannot help but let tears flow profusely, grieving for my ignorance in the past and moved by [the realization of the truth].
Regarding the Great Being’s deliverance: reflecting upon the days when turbid wisdom causes one to transmigrate, there are not few who share these same failings with me.
I have respectfully drawn from the *Daśacakrakṣitigarbha-sūtra* and the two scriptures on the *Samantabhadra-caryā-praṇidhāna* and the *Jiancha-jing*, and herein set forth this ritual method.

It is my hope that together we may cleanse our past transgressions and strive to attain future fruition; thus, shall we not ultimately remain in a state of helpless wandering? [Until] one has ascended to the stage of non-...
Those born into the state of correctness may all practice this, regardless of whether they are beginners or long-standing students.
Recorded by the Bodhisattva Śrāmaṇera Zhixu in the Fangwang Room of the Mantra Altar at Jiuzi Biefeng,
on the tenth day prior to the *svairacarya* ceremony following the Dingshou year of the Chongzhen era.
